chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar, from Maymun ibn Yusuf al-Nakhkhas, from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, who said:

I wrote asking about the times of salat (prayer), and he replied: When the sun declines, then perform your supererogatory prayer, and I prefer that your completion of the obligatory prayer be when the sun is at two feet. Then perform your supererogatory prayer, and I prefer that your completion of the ʿasr prayer be when the sun is at four feet. So if some matter presses upon you, then begin with the two obligatory prayers and make up the nawafil after them. And when the dawn rises, then perform the obligatory prayer, then make up afterward whatever you wish.

As for what is contained in the reports we presented earlier, that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of the obligatory prayer, it is to be understood as meaning that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer whose time has become restricted, or during the time of an obligatory prayer in which performing the nafilah is not permitted, as we explained: when two feet, or one and a half feet, have passed from zawal, then there is no nafilah, and one should begin with the obligatory prayer. On this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the middle of the sky
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the rise of dawn, marking the time of the morning prayer
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian, marking the beginning of zuhr time
key_terms.سُبْحَتَكَ: your supererogatory prayer before or associated with the obligatory salat

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the timing of zuhr and ʿasr prayers and when nawafil may be performed?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timings of the noon and afternoon salat (prayer), the place of nawafil in relation to the obligatory prayers, and what should be done when time is tight or an urgent matter arises. It also clarifies how reports forbidding supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer are to be understood, reconciling them with reports that allow nawafil before the obligatory salat.
